 Lakers' hot start reminiscent of past glory days
 Los Angeles' 12-2 record marks just the fifth time since 2000 they have won at least 12 of their first 14 games.
 Ian Dardani, for NBA.com
 November 17, 2026 7:20 PM Luka Dončić is leading the Lakers who are posting an NBA-best 122.8 ppg.
 Tied with the Spurs at 12-2 are the Lakers, marking just the fifth time since 2000 that Los Angeles has won at least 12 of its first 14 games.
 Those previous four instances have led to some pretty decent results:
 2001-02: 13-1 start – won NBA title 
 2008-09: 13-1 start – won NBA title 
 2010-11: 12-2 start – lost W. Conf. Semis 
 2019-20: 12-2 start – won NBA title 
 Now riding an eight-game win streak, the Purple & Gold will look to make it nine, hosting the Hornets to cap NBC’s Coast 2 Coast Tuesday ( 8 PT ).
 Luka Dončić is on a special tear as the Lakers are pouring in an NBA-best 122.8 ppg. But like San Antonio, much of their offensive success starts on the other end.
 And for L.A., disruption is the name of the game.
 Only one team ranks in the top three in both steals and blocks this season: Los Angeles.
 The Lakers boast the NBA’s best offensive rating but sit just 17th defensively. Yet they’ve made their money as an opportunistic defense, playing to Dončić’s strengths.
 The Philosophy: When you have a generational playmaker, the more possessions, the better. L.A. has embraced that approach, jumping from 22nd in total possessions last season to 7th this year (entering Monday)
 The Patience: But more possessions doesn’t mean rushing shots. With Luka operating, the Lakers are willing to work deep into the shot clock, ranking in the top eight in both ‘ late ‘ and ‘ very late ‘ shot frequency
 The Pressure: Instead, they win the possession battle by creating chaos defensively, leading the NBA in steals (11.0) and ranking 3rd in both forced turnovers (18.4) and blocks (6.4)
 “We’re building a real identity of being a disruptive basketball team,” said Lakers head coach JJ Redick postgame. “The disruptiveness is part of who we are … and it’s a big part of what’s helping us win.”
 Another Lakers steal, another Luka bucket.
 That disruption extends throughout the roster as seven different Lakers are averaging at least one steal per game, while no other team has more than five (min. 10 GP). And the offense has taken advantage, with Los Angeles scoring an NBA-best 24.4 ppg off turnovers.
 That’s led to historic results, as L.A. is just the second team since 1980 to average 120+ ppg while tallying 150+ steals and 80+ blocks through the first 14 games of a season.
 The first? The 1982-83 Showtime Lakers.
